current.text: Powell plays for Chicago this season. He signed a two-year deal with a team option in the second year, which makes him easy to trade.
He is in the projected Bulls starting five with Josh Giddey, Matas Buzelis, Caleb Wilson and Nick Claxton. He is the team's main off-ball shooter on a roster that lacks shooting.
Nikola Vucevic and Coby White left Chicago, which frees up usage. The other Bulls scorers are low-usage players.
Experts expect him to get usage in the high 20s and possibly lead the Bulls in usage all season unless he is traded.
A 2026-10-12 note says the Bulls are feeding usage to rookie Caleb Wilson.
The Chicago front office signs older players on short deals and hopes to trade them.
Trade risk is real. A trade to a better team where he is the third option would cut his usage and could collapse his value by the fantasy playoffs.
Experts value him around 70th to 90th overall, a round 7 to 8 pick, with more downside than upside. They call an ESPN-type rank near 64 or 65 too high and say to avoid him there.
In an auction mock, Josh valued him at 6 to 7 USD and called him basically the best pick of the draft at 3 USD.
His range of outcomes runs from about 40th in the best case to about 136th in the worst case.
Chicago projects as a bad team, likely bottom 10. It has a new coach, Tiago Splitter, and should play an up-tempo transition style.
Chicago has 15 back-to-backs, one below the maximum. It plays 10 games in our fantasy playoff weeks 19 to 21 (3-3-4). The first 20 games are a tough stretch.

durable.text: His fantasy value depends entirely on high usage. He puts up big numbers when he has the ball to himself and fades when he shares it with a good player.
He gives only points and threes. He adds little in rebounds, assists and blocks.
He is good at getting to the free-throw line.
He is not a point guard and is not a strong ball handler.
His value rests on his shooting. In the last two to three months of last season he shot 33% from three, his free throws fell below 80%, and he dropped outside the top 150.
Because he only scores, an off shooting year hurts his value badly. Hayes says 20 points on about 15 shots is not tremendous value.

note: Powell is a points and threes scorer. His projections show 22.3 points and 2.9 threes per game (z +1.4 and +1.5), with nothing flagged weak. He should be Chicago's top usage option unless he is traded before the 2027-03-04 deadline. Experts see him around 80th, which is near Yahoo's rank of 89 and below ESPN's 67, so target him at 3 to 7 USD (Yahoo value 7 USD, ESPN 6 USD, 8 USD in our league last year) and do not chase him at an ESPN-type price. Early in the season, check his usage share next to Caleb Wilson, his three-point and free-throw shooting, and any trade talk. A move to a contender would cut his value before our playoffs.
